Implementation Plan

Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: make the e2e-smoke-test Phase 3b implement-run probe follow the run that is doing the work (issue #8347, second delivery)

**Planning ref:** `git rev-parse HEAD` = `32ab933084172e86081c411a847fce9cc4f826b8`, branch `stable` (`heads/stable`). `Integration branch mismatch: false`.

**Clarification answers applied (round 2, after PR #8353 delivered the budget fix and the single `/approved` post):**
- **Q1 → A (AD-3):** harden `scoped_implement_progress_counts` now and treat it as hardening. It no longer stops at the first page that has a match, and it prefers the newest `in_progress` run, falling back to the newest run of any status. It gets a fixture-backed test. Candidate 3 stays recorded as unconfirmed.
- **Q2 → B (AD-4):** `--queue-timeout-secs` is not pursued, because it is outside the heal scope and the 5520 s budget already covers the confirmed failure. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh` is not touched. Existing tests already pin the values on the current ref: `--completion-timeout-secs 5520`, step `timeout-minutes: 95` and job `timeout-minutes: 165` at `tests/test_validation_refresh_workflow_contract.py:172-174`. No new pin is needed.
- **Q3 → A (AD-5):** the 4500 s alt-model deadline stays as it is. Existing tests already pin `DEADLINE=$(( $(date +%s) + 4500 ))` and the `ALT_APPROVED_POSTED` single-post flag at `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_alt_model_cleanup_pr_selector.py:174-176`. No new pin is needed.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends scoped_implement_progress_counts and the STUB_GH / _phase_step_script harness in test_test_and_mark_stable_plan_polling_guard.py
Scope-mode justification: Q2 and Q3 close their items, so the only remaining work is the Q1 hardening: one shell function inside the heal scope (`.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`), its tests under `tests/**`, and a changelog fragment. The plan reuses the function's own page validation jq, its `|| return 1` failure paths and its 10-page cap, plus the existing stub `gh` harness, so nothing new is built. The Boil the Lake rule (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed) adds two items, each under 30 lines with no new dependency or interface:
- The page walk stops early once a page holds an `in_progress` match (D2). This keeps the probe's extra GitHub API reads bounded (§14).
- Existing tests that only work because of the old stop-at-first-match behaviour are repaired so they still cover what they used to cover. Otherwise the change would quietly weaken coverage of the terminal walk and the check of a known active run by its ID.

## Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`
- `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_impl_progress_active_run.py` (new)

## Functions or modules to implement

**1. `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`, job `e2e-smoke-test`, step id `wait-implement`, function `scoped_implement_progress_counts` (lines 1492-1527)**

*Paging (replaces lines 1512-1519):*
- After the existing per-page validation (lines 1502-1511, unchanged), add the page's matches to the running list instead of overwriting it and breaking. For example `progress_matches=$(jq -cn --argjson acc "$progress_matches" --argjson page "$progress_summary" '$acc + $page.matches') || return 1`.
- Stop the walk only when one of these holds:
  - (a) The page just read has a match with `status == "in_progress"` (D2). Pages come back newest first, so the first `in_progress` match seen is the newest one, and an older page cannot change which run is picked.
  - (b) `progress_count -lt 100` (a short page).
  - (c) `progress_page` goes past `SCOPED_RUN_LOOKUP_MAX_PAGES`. This is the existing `while` bound, and the cap still returns 0 with whatever matches were collected, as today.
- Keep every `|| return 1` path. An unreadable or malformed page, including a later page after page 1 had a match, still returns 1. The caller at lines 1574-1575 then resets everything to `0/unknown`.

*Selection (replaces lines 1523-1525):*
- Compute one selected run: `(map(select(.status == "in_progress")) | sort_by(.created_at) | last) // (sort_by(.created_at) | last) // {}`.
- Set `IMPL_RUN_STATUS`, `IMPL_RUN_ID_LATEST` and `IMPL_RUN_CONCLUSION_LATEST` all from that run, keeping the existing defaults (`// "unknown"`, `// empty`, `// "unknown"`) and the existing `|| VAR=default` fallbacks.
- The fallback keeps today's `sort_by(.created_at) | last` exactly, ties included, so nothing changes when no run is `in_progress`.
- The new value goes in a new `local progress_selected`. A grep of the repo found no `progress_selected` anywhere.

*Unchanged:*
- `IMPL_RUN_TOTAL` and `IMPL_RUN_IN_PROGRESS` keep their jq; they now count every match collected.
- The consumers at 1580, 1589-1598, 1616, 1659 and 1671.
- No exported identifier is added or renamed.

*Comment (lines 1484-1491):*
- Rewrite it to say the walk goes past pages that have matches, stopping at an `in_progress` match, a short page or the cap.
- Say the probe follows the newest `in_progress` run, falling back to the newest of any status, so a duplicate `/approved` run waiting in the `ai-implement-<repo>-<issue>` concurrency group cannot hide the working run (release gate run 40831286935: `latest: pending` from 08:37 to 09:07 while `ai:implementing` was set).
- Keep the issue #7968 / run 39926633796 text and the sentence about unreadable or malformed pages.

**2. Size check.** The function grows by about 0.6–1 KB. Run `wc -c .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` and `tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py`. The file must stay below 480,000 bytes (§24).

## Data structures affected
- New shell local `progress_selected`, a JSON object holding one run.
- `progress_matches` now holds the matches collected across pages instead of one page's matches.
- No outputs, labels, env vars, log text or log prefixes change.

## API or interface changes
- None. The step outputs (`status`, `run_id`, `pr_number`), the log line formats and the function name stay the same.
- GitHub API use: when a matching page is full and has no `in_progress` run, the progress probe can now read more pages per 30-second refresh (`IMPL_PROGRESS_NEXT_READ`), still capped at `SCOPED_RUN_LOOKUP_MAX_PAGES=10` (D2).

Data flow:
1. On each poll, the 30-second throttle (line 1572) calls `scoped_implement_progress_counts`.
2. It reads page N: validate the page, add its matches to the list, then stop on an `in_progress` match, a short page or the cap. A bad page returns 1.
3. It selects one run (newest `in_progress`, else newest) and sets STATUS, ID and CONCLUSION.
4. Line 1589 reads the step name of the selected run. Line 1598 builds `CUR_STATE`, and a change in it resets the idle timer.
5. Line 1616 only runs the terminal check when TOTAL > 0 and IN_PROGRESS == 0.

Failure modes:
- **A later page is unreadable or malformed after a match on page 1.**
  - Symptom: this refresh reports `0 total / unknown`. Before, the page-1 counts were kept.
  - Recovery: the next refresh, 30 s later, reads again. Flipping between real counts and `0/unknown` changes `CUR_STATE`, so in the worst case flaky reads push the inactivity timeout back. That matches how a failed page-1 read already behaves.
- **The working run was created before `IMPL_CREATED_AFTER` (`approved_at`, line 1339/1388).** An example is a run started by the plan's own `/approved [auto-approved-by-plan]` before Phase 3a posted.
  - Symptom: no change from today, because the run is outside the `created=>` window.
  - Recovery: none in this plan (see Risks and the counterfactual).
- **10 full pages with no `in_progress` match.**
  - Behaviour: returns 0 with the matches collected so far, as the cap does today.

## Decisions

### D1 — Read pages past the first match and prefer the newest `in_progress` run
- **Chosen:** collect matches across pages and pick the newest `in_progress` match, falling back to today's newest-of-any-status.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - Only the selection change, keeping the early stop (option C in Q1).
  - No change (option B in Q1).
  - Prefer any non-completed status (`queued`/`pending`/`waiting`) as well.
- **Why:**
  - AD-3 chose this.
  - Changing selection alone cannot find a working run that sits on a later page.
  - Preferring `pending` or `queued` would bring back the exact problem, because the duplicate was `pending`.
  - The fallback keeps today's result whenever nothing is `in_progress`.

### D2 — Stop the walk at the first page that holds an `in_progress` match
- **Chosen:** stop on (a) an `in_progress` match, (b) a short page or (c) the 10-page cap.
- **Alternatives considered:** always walk until a short page or the cap, as worded in the Q1 execution plan.
- **Why:**
  - Pages are newest first, so the first `in_progress` match is the run that would be selected anyway. Reading further cannot change `IMPL_RUN_ID_LATEST` or `IMPL_RUN_STATUS`.
  - It cannot change the terminal-check decision either: `IN_PROGRESS` is already ≥ 1, so the check at line 1616 is skipped.
  - The only effect is that `IMPL_RUN_TOTAL` may leave out older runs on unread pages. That value only feeds `CUR_STATE` and the log line, and it stays the same across polls while the selection is the same.
  - It keeps the probe's GitHub API use close to today's in the common case (§14). Otherwise a busy window could cost up to 10 reads every 30 seconds, which is about 1,200 per hour against the shared `GH_PAT`.
  - Test cases (a)–(e) of the execution plan still hold exactly.

### D3 — Repair the existing tests that relied on the counter stopping at the first matching page
